extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners and patent office staff (also useful to applicants/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO guidance for conducting prior-art searches and substantive examination of patent applications, including procedural deadlines, when/what to search, how to cite prior art, outsourcing to authorized prior-art search institutes, and rules for priority claims and special applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing deadlines for reexamination and remanded applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application for which a request for reexamination is made after the decision to reject and for an application remanded from an appeal against the decision to reject, an examiner in charge shall begin the examination within one month from the receipt of the application documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination cannot start within one month due to unavoidable reasons, the reasons must be reported to the head of the examination bureau (for remanded applications) or head of examination division/team (for requests or reconsideration before trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing deadlines for expedited examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application on request of expedited examination, the examiner shall determine whether the application falls under the category of expedited examination within 7 days from receipt of the request. The examination shall begin within 2 months from delivery of the notice of the examiner’s decision (but within 4 months for expedited examination under Article 4(3) or (4) of the Directive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Instruction Article 59; the table of 'Initial Date / Time / Reference' specifies different default periods (abbreviations Month/M, Week/W, Day/D) and particular timeframes for prior-art search requests, delivery dates, and other events (e.g., 15 days, 1 month, 2 months/4 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle for law application to pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the revision of the Patent Act is made while the application is pending, transitional measures are introduced to prevent disadvantages; provisions of the law shall be applied as of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional/converted applications and applications filed by lawful right holders are deemed filed on the parent filing date, so laws are applied as of the parent filing date. International applications are governed by the filing date of the international application (not by later submissions under Article 203(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of law to priority-claiming and disclosure-exception applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application claiming the priority under Treaty or domestic priority, and an application claiming disclosure exceptions, the provisions of law shall be applied as of the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided re: internationalism and how prior public practice in another country may be treated as prior art for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of prior-art search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search for prior art is performed during the examination stage with the objective of discovering the relevant state of the art to assess patentability (novelty and inventive step). The search includes prior-filed applications prescribed in Articles 36 and 29(3) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary for examination, an examiner may outsource the search to an authorized prior-art search institute pursuant to Article 58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-search analysis of technical subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Before searching, an examiner shall analyze technical subject-matters of the invention. The search should be made on the basis of the claimed invention, but the examiner shall pay due regard to the description and drawings if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This analysis guides search strategy and selection of features to search against databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and use of documents cited in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application cites documents in the description, the examiner shall review them to determine whether they provide a starting point for the claimed invention, show the current status of the technology, explain other solutions to the task, or aid understanding of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cited documents are not directly related and merely stated in the description, the examiner shall disregard them. If necessary documents for assessing patentability cannot be acquired by common methods, the examiner shall request submission from the applicant and defer examination until submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of foreign-office/search-organization search outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If foreign patent offices or search organizations already conducted search regarding the claimed invention, the examiner shall review those search outcomes to determine whether they can be used as relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should assess the relevance and appropriateness of foreign search reports when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search scope: collections and document types to consult
rubrics_metrics.description: Search is carried out in collections/databases that are systematically accessible: primarily patent documents of various countries, supplemented by technical journals, periodicals, books, other written materials, microfiche, CD-ROM, DVD-ROM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search scope should cover all directly relevant technical fields and may be extended to analogous fields as judged by the examiner based on initial search outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When special or limited search effort is allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort is needed or search may be limited if the claimed invention falls under certain cases making meaningful search impossible or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified cases: (i) amendments include new matter under Article 47; (ii) claimed invention is not patentable under Article 32; (iii) claimed invention incomplete or not industrially applicable under Article 29; (iv) claims do not relate to one invention nor to a linked group under Article 45 (lack unity); (v) examiner is unable to understand the invention due to lack of written description. Examiner shall notify applicant that meaningful search is impossible, and may first notify grounds for rejection based on lack of unity and await response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time coverage of search (reference dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search should generally cover documents published before the filing date (or priority date for priority-claiming applications). Exceptional extension to documents published after the filing date is allowed in specific circumstances (e.g., Article 29(3)/(4) or Article 36) and when verifying priority validity is impossible at search stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents published after filing date may be used as supporting material for confirming incorrectness/incompleteness of the invention rationale or facts. For priority-claiming applications, the basic reference date for the search on each claim is the filing date of the application, but if documents exist between earliest priority date and filing date, examiner should determine reference date per claim and decide which documents to cite; examiner may set priority date per claim when straightforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of search
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may suspend the search when prior art clearly demonstrates lack of novelty or inventive step in the entire subject matter, or when completing the search would take substantial time and energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should devise the most effective method to conduct the most thorough search within available time and cost; even if rationally fails to discover effective prior arts, suspension is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle of equivalents in search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search will consider prior art incorporating technical features which are equivalents to the technical features of the claimed invention, in light of the description. Equivalent elements are not limited to features explicitly described in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a claim specifying parts joined by welding is interpreted to include other combining elements such as gluing or riveting unless the invention explicitly limits the feature to welding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search obligations for dependent claims and claim categories
rubrics_metrics.description: When searching for independent claim(s), the examiner conducts prior-art search for all dependent claims that fall within the identical classification as the independent claim. Dependent claims are interpreted as restricted by all features of the claims on which they depend. When application contains claims of different categories, all must be included in the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the independent claim's patentability is not questioned, no need to further search or cite documents for dependent claims. If a product claim is clearly novel/non-obvious, no special effort needed to search process claims inevitably resulting in that product or use claims; conversely, if only one category is present, examiner may decide to include other categories in search (examples given for pharmacological composition and method claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search based on description as well as claims (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search shall be made based on the claimed invention; nevertheless, if no additional excessive efforts are required, the examiner may conduct the search for prior art based on the invention stated in the description but not included in the claim, in case the applicant later amends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a discretionary measure to anticipate likely amendments and save rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on prior-art documents only when public availability is clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art shall be relied upon in grounds for rejection only if there are no doubts that it is publicly known/practiced or described in a distributed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prior-art document was published before the filing date in a language not understandable to the examiner, but a counterpart in an understandable language exists (even if published after filing date), the counterpart may be relied on as prior art; examiner may notify that the original-language document had been publicly known before the filing date and attach it to the notice of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of abstracts vs full texts as prior-art references
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may rely on an abstract as a prior-art reference for denying novelty and inventive step, but must notify grounds based on contents disclosed in the abstract, not on disclosure beyond the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If full text is obtainable, examiner should notify grounds based on full text. If unable to obtain full text and had to use only the abstract, notify grounds based only on the abstract. Note that differences between abstract and full text mean they cannot be treated as equal when full text is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to attach or provide access to cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of rejection must be accompanied by copies of all documents relied upon, except bulky contents for which the examiner may copy only pages directly related to the ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicants have easy Internet access (e.g., represented by agent or filed electronically), the examiner may state the URL and publication number instead of sending copies. For non-patent literature where access/copying is restricted (paid access, prohibited copy), examiner may indicate how to find references rather than attach copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unpublished prior art (another application) found during search
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner discovers prior art that is not yet laid open but considered 'another application' under Article 29(3), the examiner shall defer examination until publication; reliance on such prior art as grounds for rejection is only permitted after its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferment ensures fairness and proper public availability before using as rejection basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of prior-art relevance (X/Y/A/O/P/E/T/L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related prior art in search reports can be classified depending on relevance: X = alone destroys novelty/ inventive step; Y = requires combination with others to deny inventive step; A = related but not X or Y; O = oral disclosure/use/exhibition; P = published between international filing date and priority date; E = filed before international filing date but published after; T = documents disclosing principle/theory or published later than priority/filing date; L = may throw doubt on a priority claim or negate claimed invention or determine other contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard categorization (X, Y, A, O, P, E, T, L) when annotating citation sheets and search reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Report (ER) preparation and citation annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: After searching, the examiner prepares an Examination Report and should indicate the relevance of each cited document in the citation sheet with an X or Y annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ER may contain keywords and search history used (DB title, search formula, number of matches). Examiner may add examination references found in the search to the ER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing prior-art searches to authorized prior-art search institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO may outsource some prior-art searches under Article 58 to mitigate examiner burden, shorten processing time, improve examination quality, and protect applicants' interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsourced searches are performed by authorized institutes using formats designated by KIPO ('Search Report on Prior Art' comparing technical subject-matter of each claim with cited documents including page and line numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and request procedure for external search service
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the monthly schedule, the examiner selects applications for external search; the head of Examination Bureau confirms selection and requests the authorized institute. The Information Management Division provides selected applications to the institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heads of Patent Examination Support Division plan annual schedules and heads of Examination Bureaux allocate monthly schedules. Care must be taken not to request searches to an institute when the applicant is a searcher at that institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary review and confirmation review of outsourced search outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner conducts preliminary review before substantive examination and confirmation review after substantive examination, assessing delivery method, appropriateness of searched documents, relevancy accuracy, balanced composition among search documents, and other issues related to the search service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner produces a 'Review Statement of Prior Art Search Outcome' reporting review outcomes to division/directions and forwards to the authorized institute and Patent Examination Support Division. The service contract may obligate reexamination by the institute if outcomes are unutilized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation-review analysis report for external search outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of confirmation review during substantive examination, the examiner prepares an analysis report illustrating the utility of the external search outcomes in accordance with their practical use on the Patent Examination Processing System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This analysis documents how outsourced search outcomes were used (or not) in substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination process: notifying grounds and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application fails to satisfy prescribed requirements in the Patent Act, the examiner shall notify grounds for rejection and provide an opportunity to submit a written argument in response. If the written argument or amendment still fails to traverse the grounds, the examiner shall make a decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examination proceeds according to a defined flowchart (not shown here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the invention for examination purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall clearly understand the subject matter of the claimed invention in light of the specification by considering the problems to be solved, the means for solving the problems, how it differs from background art, and the effects of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination proceeds based on the specification as originally filed, but should take into account amendments made by the applicant prior to the notice of rejection grounds. See Part V for methods confirming amended specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should construe the claimed invention as recited in a claim. Terms in a claim should be interpreted within the general scope and meaning of the technical field, unless they have a specific meaning explicitly defined in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-interpretation of claims without logical grounds; interpret dependent claims as restricted by antecedent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of prior-art documents for publication date and technical disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall determine whether prior-art retrieved can provide grounds for rejection regarding novelty, inventive step, enlarged concept of novelty or first-to-file application; publication date is critical for determining whether it precedes filing/priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the enlarged concept of novelty, examiner shall check applicants and inventors of the prior application. Examiner must understand technical issues disclosed in the prior art and be careful not to treat as disclosed matters that are not in those documents or to over-interpret claims without logical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination for special applications (priority/disclosure/divisional/converted)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications with priority claims, disclosure exceptions, divisional, or converted applications, the examiner shall conduct formalities examination concerning validity of priority claims or procedures prior to substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If priority/domestic/disclosure claims are not compliant, examiner shall request amendment and may invalidate the procedure if deficiency not amended. For divisional/converted applications not meeting requirements for applicants or filing period, examiner shall give applicant opportunity to explain and may return documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim under treaty: eligibility and evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can claim priority under the treaty is the applicant who filed in the State party or legitimate successor. Examiner may request evidential documents proving legitimacy when applicants do not coincide. Priority claim must be made within 12 months from earliest filing date of the basis application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidential documents are not submitted within one year and four months from earliest filing date, the priority claim loses effect. Procedural amendment after statutory period cannot cure the deficiency. Copies of description/drawings from first country may be exempt if online exchange systems exist between countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-date determination for priority-claiming applications (claim-by-claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention claimed is identical (including substantially identical) to the invention of the application filed in the first country, the reference date shall be the filing date of that first-country application. For inventions not described in the first-country application, the filing date of the claiming application is the reference date. Reference date determination is in principle claim-by-claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple priority claims, earliest filing date among the relevant first-country applications governs for commonly described inventions. Combining technical matters across multiple first-country applications is treated as 'not described' in the first-country application for reference-date purposes. If the first-country application itself claims priority based on an earlier application, it may not be regarded as the 'earliest application' per Paris Convention Article 4C(2), and the examiner should specify reason for non-retroactive application when applicable.
